title: LET MY PEOPLE GO TO WORSHIP

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and say to him, 'This is what the Lord says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me. If you refuse to let them go, I will send a plague of frogs on your whole country.'"" - Exodus 8:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Again the same message, and again the same reason: let my people go, so that they may worship me.

God keeps repeating the purpose because it is easy to forget. Israel is not being rescued simply to be comfortable, or even simply to be free. They are being rescued so that they can belong to God and worship Him.

That reframes our salvation too. We were not saved merely to escape judgement, or to have better lives, or to feel peaceful. Peter says we were called out of darkness so that we might declare the praises of the One who called us (1 Pet 2:9).

Notice also the pattern of God's dealings: a clear command, followed by a clear consequence. If you refuse. Pharaoh is never ambushed. He is always told in advance.

God is not looking for excuses to judge. He is repeatedly giving opportunities to repent.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I think of my salvation mainly as rescue, or as being made a worshipper?
2. Is there a clear command of God I have been refusing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You saved me for Yourself, not just from trouble. Make my whole life an act of worship today. Amen.
